search_log: Searched "Nicholas Sparks At First Sight excerpt chapter one" and "At First Sight Nicholas Sparks read excerpt publisher"; found and opened the official Nicholas Sparks PDF excerpt.
Searched "At First Sight Nicholas Sparks point of view third person narrator", "third person", "third-person", and "narration point of view"; found an explicit but anonymous Teen Ink description.
Searched for Google Books and opened its preview and chapter links; bibliographic data and contents were accessible, but the selected preview pages supplied no diagnostic prose.

Searched exact interior phrases including "there was always a but", "Jeremy figured it was called faith", and "He didn't believe in a God who sifted through prayers"; Goodreads confirmed attribution, while Bookey supplied chapter-labeled interior third-person passages.
Opened the Nicholas Sparks work page, Hachette/Little, Brown listing, and Publishers Weekly review; they verified the work and plot but their synopsis grammar was not treated as narrator evidence.
Searched for epistolary, diary, frame, multiple-narrator, and alternating-POV indications; found no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, chiefly focalized through Jeremy: several event quotes externally name or pronominalize him while reporting his cognition, and the authorized sustained opening does the same. Chapter-labeled interior passages indicate that this pattern continues beyond the opening, while a whole-book review explicitly calls the novel third person. First- and second-person forms in the supplied quotations occur only in dialogue or generic maxims, not autonomous narrative sections. The strongest web excerpt covers only the opening, but independent interior quote evidence corroborates it; no alternating structure was found.
